name: UIAspectRatioConstraint
simple: A UIAspectRatioConstraint keeps its parent's shape the same, no matter the screen size. You give it a width-to-height ratio: 1 for a perfect square, 2 for twice as wide as tall, and so on. Great for keeping pictures and buttons from getting squished on different devices.
analogy: It's like a photo frame that can grow or shrink, but always stays the same shape, so the picture never looks stretched.
whenToUse: Keeping square icons square on phones and wide monitors
Stopping images from stretching when you size them with Scale
Keeping a panel at a nice 16:9 or 4:3 shape
where: Put it inside the UI object whose shape you want to lock. Create in Studio or with Instance.new in a LocalScript.

terms.modifier: A small invisible object you put INSIDE a UI object to change how it looks or behaves. It does nothing on its own.
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside. A modifier affects its parent.
terms.sibling: Objects that share the same parent, like brothers and sisters.
terms.UDim: Half of a UDim2: just one Scale and one Offset. UDim.new(0, 8) means 0% + 8 pixels. UDim.new(0.1, 0) means 10% of the parent's size.
terms.Scale: A fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size. 0.5 = half.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.Vector2: Two numbers together: X (width or left-right) and Y (height or up-down).
terms.aspect ratio: Width divided by height. A 200x100 box has an aspect ratio of 2. A square has 1.
terms.constraint: A rule that limits something. Here it limits the shape.
terms.axis: A direction: X is width, Y is height.
terms.AbsoluteSize: The real size in pixels after all the math.

examples.title: Keep an icon perfectly square
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

local icon = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
icon.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.15, 0.15) -- 15% of the screen width and height
icon.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.02, 0.02)
icon.Image = "rbxassetid://1234567890" -- replace with your image ID
icon.Parent = screenGui

local ratio = Instance.new("UIAspectRatioConstraint")
ratio.AspectRatio = 1 -- width = height
ratio.Parent = icon
explain: Without the constraint, on a 1000x600 screen the icon would be 150 x 90 pixels, a squished rectangle.
With AspectRatio 1, it shrinks the long side to match: 90 x 90 pixels, a perfect square.
On a tall phone screen it still stays square.

gotchas: AspectRatio is width / height. 2 means twice as WIDE. For twice as TALL use 0.5.
It overrides list and grid layouts' sizing for that item.
The constraint makes things smaller to fit the shape, so your object may end up smaller than its Size.

UIAspectRatioConstraint.AspectRatio.simple: The shape to keep, as width divided by height. 1 = square, 2 = twice as wide as tall (e.g. 200x100), 0.5 = twice as tall as wide. Must be more than 0. 16:9 widescreen is 16/9, about 1.78.
UIAspectRatioConstraint.AspectRatio.example:
local ratio = script.Parent -- a UIAspectRatioConstraint
ratio.AspectRatio = 16 / 9 -- widescreen shape

UIAspectRatioConstraint.AspectType.simple: How big the object can get while keeping its shape. FitWithinMaxSize (default) = as big as possible inside its own Size. ScaleWithParentSize = as big as possible inside its parent.

UIAspectRatioConstraint.DominantAxis.simple: Which side wins when fixing the shape: Width (default) keeps the width and changes the height to match, Height keeps the height and changes the width.
